input.summary:
room-17 "P2 living and dining" now places nothing: its 16 writes were all refused because shell-west claims every interior cell (x36..43, z14..17, y2..4) as air. The layout is kept commented in parts/room-17.mjs, and the off-palette count is 0.
make.sh now exits 0 and writes build.nbt (5948 cells), and the room-17 line shows neither REFUSED nor OFF-PALETTE.
The room is empty until shell-west (plot 2 interior fill) stops claiming its interior; then restore the layout (uncomment, add the import back).
left: The room is unfurnished: parts/room-17.mjs builds nothing, and the layout is held back as commented code (the import and the layers() call go back together).

Root cause is in shell-west.mjs line 16: its interior fill sets air over every house's interior, so runParts refuses all room writes (air included). This is outside room-17 and must be fixed by the shell's owner: leave interior cells unclaimed, or let room parts claim them.
The same lock will block the other rooms once they are filled: they are empty stubs now (placed 0, refused 0), but each room box is fully claimed by the shell.
No problems for later parts from this part: the build is whole and the palette check is clean.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owned the 16 refused cells: I re-ran build.mjs with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and wrote a script to map each cell to its owner.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one ad hoc owner-map script
waste.tool: runParts' REFUSED line should name the owning part per cell (e.g. 'claimed by shell west'). The current 'had: air' hides why the write was refused.

waste.what: Working out that the whole room box (96 cells) was claimed as air, so no layout could fit: I hand-mapped the cells with a second script.
waste.cost: one more script run and a 12-row grid by hand
waste.tool: A preflight per room box: `mcd plan` or runParts reporting free (unclaimed) cells in each room box before the part runs, e.g. '0 of 96 free'.

waste.what: Checking whether the other 54 room parts were stubs: I summarised the parts report by script.
waste.tool: runParts' report could flag parts that place 0 and refuse 0 as stubs in its one-line summary.

waste.what: Holding the layout back: the file had to be rewritten so every line of the layout was commented.
waste.cost: one Edit that left the body live, then a full Write
waste.tool: A layers() option that writes nothing and returns the planned cells (or a hold flag), so a held layout is kept as data rather than as commented code.

companions.task: Stop shell-west.mjs from filling house interiors with air, or hand the room boxes to the room parts unclaimed. This is the fix that lets room-17's layout (and the other rooms' furniture) land.
